tool_input.message:
Reviewed `git -C .claude/worktrees/mcp-serve diff main..HEAD` for beadle. The core fix is correct: `internal/daemon/templates.go:83` changes the `ethos` registry entry's args from `{"mcp"}` (a subcommand `ethos` has never had) to `{"serve"}`, matching how `ethos serve` is invoked elsewhere (e.g. `.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md`). Good fix, well-documented commit intent.

**One high-confidence bug (90) in the new test itself**, `internal/daemon/templates_test.go:149-176`, `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal`:

The test loops over every stdio entry in `DefaultMCPRegistry()` — `ethos`, `beadle-email`, and `biff` — and calls `exec.LookPath(cfg.Command)`, failing the test if the binary isn't on PATH. But only `ethos` has toolchain support for this: the Makefile's `tools-ethos` target (`Makefile:120-121`) is a `test` dependency (`Makefile:141`) and CI explicitly installs it and adds `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` to `$GITHUB_PATH` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:37-41`).

`beadle-email` and `biff` have no equivalent provisioning:
- No `tools-biff` Make target exists anywhere in the Makefile.
- `beadle-email`'s own `make build`/`make install` targets are never invoked by `make test` or CI before tests run (`Makefile:152-160` are separate, uninvoked targets).
- CI's `test.yml` workflow has no step that builds or installs either binary onto PATH.

So on a clean CI runner (and on a dev machine that hasn't manually built/installed both), `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal/beadle-email` and `.../biff` will fail with "command ... not found on PATH" — the exact `t.Fatalf` on templates_test.go:158 — even though nothing is actually wrong with those registry entries. This test currently cannot pass in CI as submitted.

Fix options: either (a) provision `beadle-email` (self-build via `go build ./cmd/beadle-email`) and `biff` (a `tools-biff` target, mirroring `tools-ethos`) as `test`/CI dependencies the same way `ethos` is, or (b) narrow the test to only the entries that have such provisioning today (just `ethos`), with a comment noting why the others are excluded, until their toolchain support exists.
